_doc: Search MATCHING contract: what counts as a match for a typed query, across every search surface. Asserted today by frontend/src/utils/searchMatch.test.ts against frontend/src/utils/searchMatch.ts. The Python/SQLite search core (docs/design-search.md D1) must assert this same file when it lands, so a query finds the same quotes in the browser, the Mac app and the CLI. Rules: docs/design-search.md §3.
_how_to_use: `match` cases: `query` is what the researcher typed; `match` is whether `text` matches; `marked` is the list of substrings of `text` that a highlight wraps, in text order. Marks are given as the marked TEXT, not as offsets, because JavaScript counts UTF-16 units and Python counts code points. `active` cases: whether a query is long enough to filter by. `known_limits` are asserted too: they record behaviour we have accepted, so a future implementation cannot change it silently in either direction.
active: one Latin letter is not enough
two letters are (changed from three on 3 Oct 2026)

one Chinese character is a word
Korean spaces its words, so it follows the Latin rule

a ligature counts as its two letters
one Japanese kana with a voicing mark
one Thai letter is not enough
apostrophes alone are not a search
an edge apostrophe is dropped, leaving one letter
one Thai vowel is one letter, though it decomposes to a mark and a vowel

_python_notes: When the Python core asserts this file, three defaults differ from JavaScript and must not be used as-is: str.lower() is final-sigma-aware while this contract folds every sigma to σ; re's \w includes the underscore while a word here is letters, digits and combining marks; and the stdlib re has no Unicode Script property, so the scripts named in searchMatch.ts (accented: Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, Arabic, Hebrew; unspaced: Han, Hiragana, Katakana, Thai) need the `regex` package or explicit ranges. Whitespace is JavaScript's \s plus U+0085, with U+FEFF treated as invisible. Since 3 Oct 2026 also: decompose (NFKD) BEFORE case folding so compatibility capitals fold ('™' is 'tm'); fold double quote marks (" “ ” „ « » 「 」) to a space; drop format characters AND variation selectors (U+FE0F); treat a letter of Han, Hiragana, Katakana or Thai before or after a word as a word boundary; and widen a highlight to whole extended grapheme clusters (the stdlib cannot: use `regex`'s \X).
